title: Existence of a composition series
statement:
Every nonzero finite-dimensional Weil representation has a
composition series.

proof.text:
We argue by induction on $\dim V$. If $V$ is simple in the sense of
[def-mg-weil-composition-series], then $0\subsetneq V$ is a composition
series. Otherwise choose a nonzero proper Weil-stable subspace
$U\subsetneq V$. Both $U$ and $V/U$ have smaller dimension, so the
induction hypothesis gives composition series for them. Taking inverse
images in $V$ of the terms in the series for $V/U$, and placing these
after the series for $U$, gives a series of the form required in
[def-mg-weil-composition-series].

lean.statement: theorem exists_compositionSeries [FiniteDimensional k V] : Nonempty ρ.CompositionSeries
lean.note: The upstream declaration explicitly carries this blueprint id and applies to the given Weil representation by taking W to be its Weil group. Its CompositionSeries is a finite chain of invariant subspaces from bottom to top with covering steps, equivalently nonzero simple successive quotients by Subrepresentation.isIrreducible_subquotient_iff and Representation.isIrreducible_iff. The existing theorem also handles the zero representation; the node is its restriction to nonzero Weil representations. No new definition or duplicate existence theorem is introduced.
